c_page_sub: See what your line actually did, keep every complaint in one place, and send the provider or regulator a message backed by your own measurements.
c_profile_sub: Shown at the top of the monthly report. Stays on this computer.
c_plan_hint: The speed your contract promises. The report compares your speed tests with it.
c_empty: No complaints yet. When you call your provider, write down the complaint number here.
c_ticket_ph: The number the agent gave you
c_notes_ph: What happened, what they promised, when they said it would be fixed…
c_delete_body: It will be removed from this list and from future reports.
c_overdue: The provider's response window has passed with no fix. You can escalate to {regulator} now.
c_err_ticket: Enter the complaint number or a note
c_guide_1: Complain to your provider first and write down the complaint number, date and agent name.
c_guide_2: Give them {window} to fix it. Keep Internet Monitor running so every drop in that time is recorded.
c_guide_4: Open the complaint below, copy the ready-made text and attach the evidence ZIP. Every file in it has a SHA-256 checksum so anyone can confirm nothing was edited.
c_guide_note: Rules differ between countries and can change. Check your regulator's website for the exact steps.
c_reg_gb: your provider's ADR scheme (Communications Ombudsman or CISAS)
c_g3_eg: If it isn't fixed, escalate to the National Telecom Regulatory Authority (NTRA): call 155, use the My NTRA app, or its online complaints portal. Have your landline number and the provider's complaint number ready.
c_g3_sa: If it isn't fixed, escalate to the Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST) through its website or app, with the provider's complaint number.
c_g3_gb: If it isn't fixed after 8 weeks, or the provider sends a deadlock letter, take it to the free ADR scheme your provider belongs to (Communications Ombudsman or CISAS). If the line is completely down for more than 2 working days, Ofcom's automatic compensation applies.
c_g3_us: File an informal complaint with the FCC at fcc.gov/complaints. The FCC sends it to the provider, which has to reply within 30 days.
c_g3_other: If it isn't fixed, escalate to your country's telecom regulator. Most accept complaints online with the provider's complaint number.
c_response: Days the provider has to respond
c_response_hint: Leave empty to use {window}, the usual rule in {country}.
